R001.fact: If a vector space W over a field has finite dimension n and (u_i) indexed by a finite set J of cardinality n is linearly independent, then this family is a basis of W.

grounds.reason: H004 supplies dim_C V=lambda+1.
Before the dimension step, S002 proves |I|=lambda+1=n and independence of (e_i) by the displayed coefficient-isolation argument.

R001.justification: Start with a basis of n vectors, which exists by the given finite dimension. Insert the independent u_i one by one: expansion of the next u_i in the current basis has a nonzero coefficient on a basis vector outside the previously inserted vectors, since otherwise independence would fail. Solve for that basis vector and exchange it for u_i; spanning and independence are preserved. After n such exchanges the basis consists exactly of the u_i. Apply this with W=V, J=I and u_i=e_i.

R001.fact: For natural m,r, with 0!=1 and an empty product equal to 1, product_{a=1}^r(m+a)/r! = binom(m+r,r) is a nonnegative integer. Here binom(N,r), for 0<=r<=N, is the number of r-element subsets of an N-element set, equivalently N!/(r!(N-r)!). Every natural factorial is a positive integer and hence is nonzero as a complex scalar.

grounds.reason: H003 gives integer lambda>=0.
D005 gives 0<=i<=lambda for i in I.
r is an arbitrary natural number.
The x coefficient has m=lambda-i>=0; the y coefficient has m=i>=0, in exactly the stated branches.

R001.justification: For N=m+r, ordered selections of r distinct elements from an N-element set number N(N-1)...(N-r+1). Each r-element subset has exactly r! such orderings. Thus this product divided by r! is the integer subset count; reversing its factors gives (m+1)...(m+r)/r!. For r=0 both counts and products equal 1. Factorial positivity follows by induction from 0!=1 and (s+1)!=(s+1)s!. These facts justify the two binomial identifications and integrality. The remaining generator coefficients lambda-i+1, i+1 and lambda-2i are visibly integers, and the zero branches have integer coefficient zero.

R002.fact: Since V has the finite complex basis (e_i) indexed by I with |I|=n, every complex basis of V has n vectors. Consequently H007's simultaneous integer/complex basis can be indexed by I.

grounds.reason: N001 gives a complex basis with n elements.
H007 supplies a basis of M that is also a complex basis of V.

R002.justification: Finite basis exchange bounds any linearly independent family by the size of a finite spanning family: successively replace a spanning vector by each independent vector using a nonzero coordinate. Thus any basis has at most n elements; applying the same bound in the opposite direction gives exactly n. Reindex by a bijection with I.

R002.fact: For the chosen integer basis (a_i) indexed by finite I, the maps R^I -> R tensor_Z M, d -> sum_i d_i tensor a_i, and r tensor m -> (r c_i(m))_i are inverse R-linear maps, where c_i are the integer coordinate maps. Under iota, d maps to sum_i d_i a_i, and this map is injective because (a_i) is complex-linearly independent and R is a subring of C.

grounds.reason: F001 supplies the simultaneous integer/complex basis.
R is included in Q and C.
M_R is the indicated tensor product.
iota acts on pure tensors by multiplication.

R002.justification: The integer coordinates are additive, so (r,m) -> (r c_i(m)) is Z-balanced and induces the stated tensor map. The composites are identity on coordinate vectors and on pure tensors, since m=sum_i c_i(m)a_i; these generate the respective modules. Complex independence then forces every coefficient of a zero image to vanish. Hence the displayed images are an R-basis, and their complex span is V.

R002.fact: For prime integer p and integers 0<=j<=lambda<p, p divides none of lambda!, j!, (lambda-j)! or binom(lambda,j). Hence binom(lambda,j) is a unit of Z_(p), with inverse 1/binom(lambda,j).

grounds.reason: p is prime.
0<=lambda<p.
j in I means 0<=j<=lambda.
A rational with denominator prime to p belongs to R.

R002.justification: Each positive factorial factor is less than p. A prime dividing a finite product divides a factor, so none of these factorials is divisible by p; 0!=1 covers the endpoints. This prime product property follows from Bezout for a factor coprime to p. The integer identity lambda!=binom(lambda,j)j!(lambda-j)! then excludes divisibility of the binomial coefficient. It is a positive integer, lies in R, and its reciprocal has denominator prime to p.

R002.fact: For the complex basis (e_i) indexed by I, equality of linear operators is determined by their values on all e_i, and the defined matrix units satisfy E_ab E_cd=delta_(b,c) E_ad. In particular E_(lambda,lambda)^2=E_(lambda,lambda) and E_(i,lambda)E_(lambda,j)=E_ij.

grounds.reason: The e_i form a complex basis.
D010 defines each matrix unit by its values on that basis.
F003 identifies Q and the two adjacent operator products.

R002.justification: On e_k, E_cd gives zero unless k=d, in which case it gives e_c. Applying E_ab gives e_a exactly when also c=b, and otherwise zero. Thus the asserted products have equal values on every basis vector. Linear extension proves both the product identities and the criterion for operator equality.

R003.fact: For an R-submodule J of C with R=Z_(p) contained in Q, multiplication defines a Q-linear map Q tensor_R J -> C. Every tensor is (1/d) tensor c for a nonzero integer d and c in J; hence this map is injective and has image the Q-linear span of J. A finite R-generating list of J becomes a Q-spanning list. An R-linear decomposition M_R isomorphic to the finite product J^I induces the corresponding Q-linear decomposition after tensoring.

grounds.reason: R is a subring of Q with its specified scalar inclusion into C.
F001 gives the R-submodule J, finite generation and finite coordinate decomposition.
iota and the coordinate identifications respect the specified R-action.

R003.justification: The map (q,c) -> qc is R-balanced. Write a tensor as a finite sum q_l tensor c_l and choose a nonzero integer d with d q_l integral. Balancing gives (1/d) tensor sum_l (d q_l)c_l. Its zero product forces the second factor to vanish in C. The image consists exactly of finite rational sums of elements of J. Balancing likewise makes a finite generating list span after tensoring. Tensor the coordinate maps and their inclusions; their composites are identities on pure tensors and thus on the whole tensor product. Finiteness of I permits adding all coordinate inclusions.

R003.fact: R=Z_(p) and Q satisfy the strong rank condition. A vector space with a finite spanning list has a finite basis; linear isomorphisms preserve its finite dimension. Over a ring with the strong rank condition a free module with an n-element basis has finrank n.

grounds.reason: Primality ensures the indicated localization is a subring domain of Q.
Z is contained in R, R is contained in Q, and every rational is a quotient of elements of R.
M_R is free over R of rank n.
n is positive and I has n elements.
F002 gives finite dimensionality of T and the Q-linear isomorphism used in the rank comparison.

R003.justification: For an injective R-linear map R^a -> R^b, extend its matrix to Q. A nonzero vector in the kernel over Q could be multiplied by a common nonzero integer denominator to give a nonzero kernel vector over R, a contradiction. Thus the extension is injective and a<=b by finite linear algebra. Over Q the same inequality follows by elimination on a matrix. From a finite spanning list delete each vector dependent on the retained vectors; the resulting independent spanning list is a basis. Isomorphisms carry bases to bases, and finite basis cardinality is invariant by the injective dimension inequality. This also identifies natural-valued module rank with n for a finite free basis.

R003.fact: For prime integer p and every nonzero rational q, there exist eta in Z and a unit u of R=Z_(p) such that q=p^eta u. For a nonempty finite family of such exponents, its minimum nu is attained, and p^(eta_j-nu) belongs to R for each j.

grounds.reason: p is prime, hence p>=2 and p is nonzero.
Fractions with denominator prime to p are exactly the given elements of R.
The coefficients are nonzero rational numbers in a nonempty finite generating list.

R003.justification: Write q=A/B with nonzero integers A,B. Repeatedly remove factors p from A and B; this terminates because their nonzero absolute values decrease at each division by p>=2. Write A=p^s A' and B=p^t B', with A',B' prime to p. Then eta=s-t and u=A'/B'; both u and its inverse lie in R. A finite nonempty list of integers has an attained minimum. Each eta_j-nu is nonnegative, so the corresponding power of p is integral and belongs to R. This verifies the factorization and minimum step already used by S004–S005.

R004.fact: For prime p, R=Z_(p), and a field K of characteristic p, the integer map uniquely extends to a unital homomorphism bar:R->K by bar(a/d)=a_K/d_K. Reduction a/d |-> [a][d]^{-1} identifies R/pR with F_p.

grounds.reason: p is prime.
K has characteristic p.
R consists of rational fractions with denominators prime to p.

R004.justification: The integer map has kernel pZ, so each allowed denominator has nonzero image. Equality of rational fractions gives equality after cross multiplication in K, proving well-definedness; fraction arithmetic proves the homomorphism laws and inverses force uniqueness. The same construction into F_p is onto via integers, and its kernel consists precisely of fractions with numerator divisible by p, namely pR.

R004.fact: With the R action on K given by bar, the displayed Phi and Psi are K-linear isomorphisms. For every additive lattice operator A:M->M, its extension A_R on R tensor_Z M and its induced quotient operator commute with these isomorphisms.

grounds.reason: M_R=R tensor_Z M.
V_K=M tensor_Z K.
The ring map and the forward/inverse pure-tensor formulas are constructed here, and R/pR=F_p.
The required operators preserve M and their restrictions are additive.

R004.justification: Phi's inverse is balanced in s,m over Z and in the outer tensor over R because multiplication by t in R becomes multiplication by bar(t) in K. Its two composites are the identity using outer balancing. For Psi's inverse, replacing u by u+pw changes u tensor c by w tensor pc=0. F_p balancing follows by choosing integer representatives. Forward R balancing follows since every s acts on M_R/pM_R by its residue in F_p. The inverse identities hold on pure tensors, which generate. Intertwining follows by applying either composite to a pure tensor: A changes only the M factor (or its class).

R004.fact: For the finite R-basis (a_i) supplied here, (a_i tensor 1) is a K-basis of M_R tensor_R K, and ([a_i]) is an F_p-basis of M_R/pM_R.

grounds.reason: N003 provides b and the R-basis with inverse images a_i.
iota is injective, identifying the stated image basis with a basis of M_R.

R004.justification: Writing u=sum_i a_i r_i, the map u tensor c |-> (bar(r_i)c)_i is balanced and inverse to (c_i)_i |-> sum_i a_i tensor c_i. Thus the displayed vectors are a basis without requiring flatness. Reducing the same unique finite coordinates identifies M_R/pM_R with (R/pR)^I. Transport through Phi gives beta and through Psi the compatible reduction basis.

R004.fact: An R-linear endomorphism A of M_R extends to A_K(u tensor c)=Au tensor c. This extension preserves sums, compositions, identities and multiplication by s in R (mapped to bar(s)); conjugation through Phi preserves these identities as well. A unit s of R has nonzero image in K and bar(s^{-1})=bar(s)^{-1}.

grounds.reason: The generator and divided-power formulas on the complex basis are explicit.
The required operators preserve iota(M_R); E_ij obey the product identity and its binomial coefficient is a unit.
Phi is an isomorphism intertwining the induced lattice operators.
a_i is the inverse image of b e_i and beta_i its transported tensor.

R004.justification: Restrictions of the complex-linear operators to the stable R-module are R-linear; injectivity of iota transfers their identities to M_R. Each assertion about scalar extension is verified on pure tensors using balancing, and hence holds on their finite sums. On a_i, complex linearity gives exactly the coefficients on e_i, including the Kronecker action of E_ij. Finally bar(s)bar(s^{-1})=1 in the nonzero field K, giving both nonvanishing and the inverse formula. Thus N002's stated E product transfers with exactly the displayed scalar and order.

R005.fact: For a K-linear subspace W of a K-vector space, the linear endomorphisms A satisfying A(W) subset W contain the identity and are closed under composition, K-scalar multiplication and finite sums. In particular, stability under A implies stability under A^r for every natural r.

grounds.reason: W is a K-linear subspace of V_K.
L1 assumes stability under x_K,y_K,h_K; the other operators are scalar compositions by N004.
All T_ij and the induced operators are K-linear endomorphisms with the displayed factorization.

R005.justification: For w in W, Bw lies in W and then A(Bw) lies in W whenever A and B preserve W. Subspace closure places a A(w) and finite sums of such vectors in W. The identity preserves W. Induction starting from the identity proves closure under each nonnegative power. These facts justify exactly the operations used in S002.

R005.fact: In the field K of characteristic prime p, if 0<=r<=lambda<p, the image of r! in K is nonzero and has a multiplicative inverse.

grounds.reason: p is prime.

R005.justification: Every integer t between 1 and r is strictly between 0 and p, so its image in a field of characteristic p is nonzero. Their finite product is nonzero since a field has no zero divisors. For r=0 the product is 1. Each resulting nonzero field element is invertible.

R005.fact: For L_K=(Zx+Zy+Zh) tensor_Z K, the elements x tensor 1, y tensor 1, h tensor 1 span L_K over K. For the K-linear representation rho, a K-linear subspace is an L_K-submodule exactly when it is invariant under x_K,y_K,h_K.

grounds.reason: D014 gives exactly this tensor construction of L_K.

R005.justification: Every tensor is a finite sum of pure tensors. For a,b,d in Z, balancing and additivity express (a x+b y+d h) tensor c as (a c)(x tensor 1)+(b c)(y tensor 1)+(d c)(h tensor 1), where integer coefficients are mapped into K. Thus every rho(z) is a K-linear combination of the three generator operators and preserves W if those operators do. Conversely, stability under all rho(z) includes these three. This is precisely the defining stability condition for a submodule.

source_steps.text: The representation carries brackets to operator commutators. H005 and H006 therefore give the following inductions. The h identity starts at hv=lambda v, and h y^(t+1)v=y h y^t v-2y^(t+1)v=(lambda-2(t+1))y^(t+1)v. For x the base t=1 is xyv=yxv+hv=lambda v. The step for t>=1 is xy^(t+1)v=yxy^t v+hy^t v=[t(lambda-t+1)+(lambda-2t)]y^t v=(t+1)(lambda-t)y^t v. In the h step L1 is the temporary hypothesis hy^t v=(lambda-2t)y^t v. In the x step for t>=1, L2 is the temporary hypothesis xy^t v=t(lambda-t+1)y^(t-1)v; its use of the h identity is justified by the completed first induction. Discharge each step hypothesis and apply natural induction. Thus F001 holds for all natural t, with the x formula used only for t>=1.

H003 gives lambda>=0, so |I|=lambda+1=n>0. Iterating F001, for i in I, x^i y^i v=i! lambda(lambda-1)...(lambda-i+1)v!=0: when i=0 the product is 1; otherwise all i factors of the descending product are positive integers and v!=0 by H006. Thus e_i!=0. To prove independence fix any coefficient family c indexed by I and temporarily assume L3: sum_(i in I)c_i e_i=0. For any j in I, apply product_(k in I,k!=j)(h-(lambda-2k)Id_V). The h formula of F001 kills every summand except j; its multiplier on e_j is product_(k!=j)2(k-j), nonzero over C. Hence c_j=0. Since j was arbitrary all coefficients vanish; discharge L3. H004 gives dim_C V=n, so the n independent vectors e_i form a basis.

Set z=y^(lambda+1)v. By F001, hz=(-lambda-2)z. Expand z in the basis F002; none of the eigenvalues lambda-2i for i in I equals -lambda-2. Applying h-(-lambda-2)Id to this expansion and using independence makes every coefficient zero, so z=0. Every higher lowering power vanishes. Dividing the identities in F001 by i! now gives xe_0=0, xe_i=(lambda-i+1)e_(i-1) for i>=1 in I, ye_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) for i<lambda, ye_lambda=0 and he_i=(lambda-2i)e_i.

Iterate F003 r times and divide by r!. If r<=i, the x coefficient is (lambda-i+1)...(lambda-i+r)/r!=binom(lambda-i+r,r). If i+r<=lambda, the y coefficient is (i+1)...(i+r)/r!=binom(i+r,r). If r>i the x string reaches xe_0=0, and if i+r>lambda the y string reaches ye_lambda=0. These are integer binomial coefficients, including r=0 where each empty product is 1. Together with F001-F003 these give all the asserted basis and operator formulas.

By H007, every X_r,Y_r preserves M. In particular x=X_1 and y=Y_1 preserve M; H005 gives h=xy-yx as operators on V, so h also preserves M. Their restrictions satisfy the same commutator identities. H001 makes R the subring obtained by inverting integers prime to p. H007 supplies an integer basis of M that is a complex basis of V; N001 gives complex dimension n and |I|=n, so that basis has n elements and can be indexed by I.

Choose such a basis a from F001. Its tensor images 1 tensor a_i form an R-basis of M_R: the integer coordinate maps of a tensor to mutually inverse maps between M_R and R^I, sending sum_(i in I) d_i tensor a_i to (d_i)_(i in I). Under iota this basis maps to a_i. If a finite R-linear combination maps to zero, its coefficients vanish by complex independence of a. Hence iota is injective, its image is the R-span of a, and M_R is free of rank n. The image complex-linearly spans V because a is a complex basis. Each X_r,Y_r is complex-linear and preserves M by F001, so preserves this R-span.

Fix i,j in I. The basis formulas in N001 give Q=Y_lambda X_lambda=E_(lambda,lambda): X_lambda kills e_k for k<lambda and sends e_lambda to e_0, which Y_lambda sends back to e_lambda. They also give X_(lambda-i)Q=E_(i,lambda), since the surviving coefficient is binom(lambda-i,lambda-i)=1. Finally Q Y_(lambda-j)=binom(lambda,j)E_(lambda,j). Indeed an input e_k with k<j goes below e_lambda and is killed by Q; for k>j it goes past the lowering string and vanishes; and e_j maps with coefficient binom(lambda,lambda-j)=binom(lambda,j). These statements include lambda=0. By H001 and H003, lambda!, j!, (lambda-j)! have no prime factor p. The factorial identity lambda!=binom(lambda,j)j!(lambda-j)! then shows p does not divide binom(lambda,j), so its rational inverse lies in R.

Composing the three identities in F003 and using the defining action of matrix units gives E_ij=binom(lambda,j)^(-1)X_(lambda-i)Y_lambda X_lambda Y_(lambda-j) for every i,j in I. All factors preserve iota(M_R) by F002, and the scalar is in R by F003, hence every E_ij preserves it. F001-F003 and this formula establish all the asserted localization and matrix-unit properties. No weights modulo p were separated.

By N001, the e_i form a basis. By N002, E_ii projects iota(M_R) onto J_i e_i and E_ij carries c e_j to c e_i while preserving iota(M_R); therefore J_j is contained in J_i for every i,j in I. Reversing indices gives equality. The set I contains 0 since n=lambda+1>0, so the common module is J. Each J_i is an R-submodule, and multiplication by e_i identifies it with the image of the R-linear projection E_ii on the finite free module iota(M_R). Images of a finite generating set generate the image, so J is finitely generated. It is nonzero: if every coordinate projection were zero, all of iota(M_R) would be zero, contradicting its complex span V and dim V=n>0. Finally a vector in iota(M_R) is the sum of its E_ii projections, all in J e_i, and conversely every such finite sum belongs to iota(M_R); independence of the e_i makes this sum direct.

Define T=Q tensor_R J. Its multiplication map mu:T->C sends q tensor c to qc. It is injective by the fraction description of localization: any element is a finite sum of pure tensors, and a common nonzero integer denominator d rewrites it as (1/d) tensor c' for some c' in J, because d times each rational coefficient belongs to Z, hence R. If its product in C vanishes, c'=0, so the tensor is zero. This also exhibits Q as the fraction field of R and realizes T as the localization of the torsion-free module J inside C. The images 1 tensor c of a finite generating set of J span T over Q, so T is finite dimensional. Tensoring the finite direct decomposition in F001 gives Q tensor_R M_R isomorphic to product_(i in I)T: the forward map consists of tensoring each coordinate c e_i -> c, and the inverse adds the coordinate inclusions c -> c e_i. On pure tensors their two composites are the identity, hence on every tensor by linearity.

Set r=dim_Q T, a finite natural number by F002. Apply M002 with source B=R, A=Q and source module M_R. N002 provides its free R-basis of n elements, so finrank_R M_R=n and M002 gives dim_Q(Q tensor_R M_R)=n. The rings R and Q are commutative domains and satisfy the strong rank condition: for R, clear denominators to preserve injectivity after passage to its fraction field Q, then apply finite-dimensional linear algebra over Q; for Q use that same dimension inequality directly. Apply M001 over Q to the constant family T indexed by I. F002 supplies finite dimensionality and hence a finite basis of T, while N001 supplies |I|=n. Thus dim_Q(T^I)=sum_(i in I)r=nr. The isomorphism in F002 now gives n=nr; n>0 by N001, whence r=1. Together with injectivity of mu, J therefore spans a one-dimensional rational line in C.

F001 and F003 imply existence of a nonzero a in J and a nonempty finite list of nonzero rational scalars q_1,...,q_k for which q_1 a,...,q_k a generate J over R: start with any nonzero a in J, use the one-dimensional rational span to express a finite generating list as rational multiples of a, and discard zero entries. Each nonzero rational q_j admits q_j=p^(eta_j)u_j with eta_j an integer and u_j a unit of R. Indeed remove the maximal powers of the prime p from the nonzero numerator and denominator; their difference is eta_j and the remaining numerator and denominator are prime to p, making both u_j and its inverse elements of R. Thus the tuple of data specified in F004 exists.

Choose a,k,q,eta,u with the properties in F004. Define nu=min_(1<=j<=k) eta_j and b=p^nu a. Every generator q_j a=p^(eta_j-nu)u_j b belongs to Rb because eta_j-nu>=0. An index attaining the minimum has q_j a=u_j b, and u_j is an R-unit, so b lies in J and this one generator generates Rb. Thus J=Rb, and b!=0 since p is a nonzero integer and a!=0. F001 now gives iota(M_R)=direct_sum_(i in I)Rb e_i. The vectors b e_i are independent by N001 and b!=0 and span by that equality, so form an R-basis. N002 makes iota an isomorphism onto its image, which supplies the equivalent R-basis of M_R. Existentially close the witnesses; together with F001-F003 this gives all the asserted coordinate-module and basis properties.

By H001-H002, an integer denominator not divisible by p has nonzero image in K and therefore an inverse. Thus the integer map extends uniquely to bar:R->K, bar(a/d)=a_K/d_K. Define Phi:V_K->M_R tensor_R K by m tensor c |-> (1 tensor m) tensor c; define its inverse on pure tensors by (s tensor m) tensor c |-> m tensor (bar(s)c). The tensor balancing relations make these well-defined K-linear maps, and their composites are the identity on pure tensors, hence on all elements. Since p maps to zero, define Psi:M_R tensor_R K -> (M_R/pM_R) tensor_(F_p) K by u tensor c |-> [u] tensor c; its inverse sends [u] tensor c to u tensor c. Changing u by p times a vector changes this by zero, and the F_p balancing relation follows from the R balancing relation and bar modulo p. Conversely R/pR=F_p because every denominator is prime to p, so every R scalar has the same reduction as an element of F_p. These maps are mutually inverse on pure tensors. N002 supplies preservation of M by all lattice operators, and H005 their Chevalley relations, so the actions rho and the operators X_K,Y_K are well-defined and all these tensor maps commute with them.

Choose b from N003, so b!=0 and the vectors b e_i form an R-basis of iota(M_R). Define a_i=iota^(-1)(b e_i) in M_R and beta_i=Phi^(-1)(a_i tensor 1) in V_K. The a_i form an R-basis by N002-N003. Its coordinate maps and the map (c_i) -> sum_i a_i tensor c_i are inverse K-linear maps between K^I and M_R tensor_R K; on each pure tensor this is precisely the coordinate expansion. Hence the beta_i form a K-basis. Likewise reducing the coordinates modulo p shows that the classes of a_i form an F_p-basis of M_R/pM_R, whose scalar extension gives this same basis via Psi. N001 gives |I|=n=lambda+1>0. Thus dim_K V_K=n>0.

N001 gives the explicit generator and divided-power actions on e. Complex linearity gives the same coefficients on b e_i, hence on a_i via iota and on beta_i after applying bar. Consequently x_K beta_0=0, x_K beta_i=(lambda-i+1)beta_(i-1) for 1<=i<=lambda, y_K beta_i=(i+1)beta_(i+1) for 0<=i<lambda, y_K beta_lambda=0, and h_K beta_i=(lambda-2i)beta_i for i in I. N002 gives preservation of iota(M_R) by E_ij. Define T_ij by the induced lattice action after pulling back through iota and extending scalars using Phi; then T_ij beta_k=beta_i if k=j and 0 otherwise. Transporting the equality E_ij=binom(lambda,j)^(-1)X_(lambda-i)Y_lambda X_lambda Y_(lambda-j) from N002 gives T_ij=bar(binom(lambda,j))^(-1)X_(lambda-i)^K Y_lambda^K X_lambda^K Y_(lambda-j)^K. This scalar is defined and nonzero, because N002 states that binom(lambda,j) is a unit of R and a unital homomorphism to a field maps units to units.

For any integer r with 0<=r<=lambda, H003 and H001 imply p does not divide r!, so H002 gives r! !=0 in K. The equality r! X_r=x^r on V restricts to the same equality on M by N002 and reduces to r! X_r^K=x_K^r on V_K. Division yields X_r^K=(r!)^(-1)x_K^r, and the identical argument gives Y_r^K=(r!)^(-1)y_K^r. F001-F003 and these formulas prove all the asserted basis, scalar-extension and operator properties, existentially closing b,a,beta,T. When lambda=0, all factorials and binomial coefficients here are 1. No assumption on algebraic closure of K has been used.

Use H001-H002 for the prime-field/scalar identifications and H005 for the Chevalley construction. N001 and N002 supply the basis-defined matrix units and the restrictions of the lattice operators used in this construction, so all definitions of rho,x_K,y_K,h_K,X_K,Y_K are guarded by established inputs. Choose a basis beta and endomorphisms T with the full properties of N004. In particular dim_K V_K=n>0, so V_K is nonzero.

Fix an arbitrary K-linear subspace W of V_K and assume L1: W is invariant under x_K,y_K,h_K. It is then invariant under each nonnegative power of x_K and y_K, including power zero, and under their K-scalar multiples. N004 gives X_r^K=(r!)^(-1)x_K^r and Y_r^K=(r!)^(-1)y_K^r for every 0<=r<=lambda. Every index lambda-i, lambda and lambda-j2 in the formula for T_(i,j2) lies in this interval, and binom(lambda,j2) is nonzero in K. Stability under composition and scalar multiplication now shows that W is invariant under every T_(i,j2), hence under all matrix units since i,j2 were arbitrary.

Split into the exhaustive cases W={0} and W!={0}. In the zero branch temporarily assume L3: W={0}; the desired disjunction follows immediately, so discharge L3 to close that branch. In the nonzero branch temporarily assume L2: W!={0}. Since beta is a basis from N004, there exist w in W, a coefficient family c in K^I, and j in I such that w!=0, w=sum_(i in I)c_i beta_i, and c_j!=0; otherwise all coefficients of every w in W would be zero. Retain this existence as F003 for the next paragraph.

Choose w,c,j from F003. For every i in I, the matrix-unit action in N004 gives T_ij w=c_j beta_i. F002 places this vector in W; division by the nonzero c_j in the field K yields beta_i in W. Thus all basis vectors belong to W and W=V_K. Discharge the nonzero-case assumption L2; together with the zero case this proves W={0} or W=V_K under L1.

Discharge L1 to conclude that invariance under x_K,y_K,h_K implies W={0} or W=V_K, and universally quantify the arbitrary subspace W. Combine this with nonzeroness from F001 to obtain the target conclusion. Since the Chevalley generators span L_K, their invariant subspaces are exactly the L_K-submodules. The endpoint lambda=0 uses a single basis vector with all relevant factorials and binomial coefficients equal to 1. By H003, for p=2 the allowed lambda values are 0 and 1, and the same formulas apply. No step separates h_K-eigenvalues or assumes K algebraically closed.

import Mathlib
universe u v
open scoped TensorProduct
open Module
attribute [local instance 100] LieRing.ofAssociativeRing
noncomputable section
namespace Reduction
def loc (p : ℕ) : Subring ℚ :=
  Subring.closure {q : ℚ | ∃ d : ℤ, ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ d ∧ q = (d : ℚ)⁻¹}
instance locComplex (p : ℕ) : Algebra (loc p) ℂ :=
  ((Rat.castHom ℂ).comp (loc p).subtype).toAlgebra
abbrev Ind (l : ℤ) := Fin (l.toNat + 1)
abbrev MR {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V] (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) :=
  (loc p) ⊗[ℤ] M
abbrev VK {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V] (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V) :=
  K ⊗[ℤ] M
variable {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
instance locModule (p : ℕ) : Module (loc p) V := Module.compHom V (algebraMap (loc p) ℂ)
instance locTower (p : ℕ) : IsScalarTower (loc p) ℂ V := ⟨fun _ _ _ => mul_smul _ _ _⟩
def iota (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : MR p M →ₗ[loc p] V :=
  LinearMap.liftBaseChange (loc p) M.subtype

abbrev SL := LieAlgebra.SpecialLinear.sl (Fin 2) ℂ
def divided (a : Module.End ℂ V) (r : ℕ) : Module.End ℂ V :=
  ((r.factorial : ℂ)⁻¹) • a ^ r
def e (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (i : ℕ) : V := divided y i v
def stable {A W : Type*} [Semiring A] [AddCommMonoid W] [Module A W]
    (U : Submodule A W) (f : Module.End A W) : Prop := ∀ w ∈ U, f w ∈ U
def matrixUnit {A W ι : Type*} [Semiring A] [AddCommMonoid W] [Module A W]
    (b : Basis ι A W) (i j : ι) : Module.End A W :=
  LinearMap.smulRight (b.coord j) (b i)
def Jcoord (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (i : ℕ) :
    Submodule (loc p) ℂ :=
  (iota p M).range.comap (LinearMap.smulRight (LinearMap.id : ℂ →ₗ[loc p] ℂ) (e y v i))
structure IntegralOps (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (M : Submodule ℤ V) where
  ix : Module.End ℤ M
  iy : Module.End ℤ M
  ih : Module.End ℤ M
  iX : ℕ → Module.End ℤ M
  iY : ℕ → Module.End ℤ M
  ix_spec : ∀ m : M, (ix m : V) = x m
  iy_spec : ∀ m : M, (iy m : V) = y m
  ih_spec : ∀ m : M, (ih m : V) = h m
  iX_spec : ∀ (r : ℕ) (m : M), (iX r m : V) = divided x r m
  iY_spec : ∀ (r : ℕ) (m : M), (iY r m : V) = divided y r m
def admissible (M : Submodule ℤ V) (x y : Module.End ℂ V) : Prop :=
  (∃ (ι : Type) (_ : Fintype ι) (a : Basis ι ℤ M) (b : Basis ι ℂ V),
    ∀ i, (a i : V) = b i) ∧
  (∀ (r : ℕ) (m : M), divided x r m ∈ M ∧ divided y r m ∈ M)
def highestModule (l : ℤ) (act : SL →ₗ⁅ℂ⁆ Module.End ℂ V) (x h : SL) : Prop :=
  FiniteDimensional ℂ V ∧ Module.finrank ℂ V = l.toNat + 1 ∧ Nontrivial V ∧
  (∀ U : Submodule ℂ V, (∀ z : SL, stable U (act z)) → U = ⊥ ∨ U = ⊤) ∧
  ∃ w : V, w ≠ 0 ∧ act x w = 0 ∧ act h w = (l : ℂ) • w
def chevalley (x y h : SL) : Prop :=
  IsSl2Triple h x y ∧ Submodule.span ℂ ({x, y, h} : Set SL) = ⊤
def strings (l : ℤ) (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) : Prop :=
  (∀ t : ℕ, h ((y ^ t) v) = ((l : ℂ) - 2 * (t : ℂ)) • (y ^ t) v) ∧
  ∀ t : ℕ, 1 ≤ t → x ((y ^ t) v) =
    ((t : ℂ) * ((l : ℂ) - (t : ℂ) + 1)) • (y ^ (t - 1)) v
def generatorFormulas {A W : Type*} [Field A] [AddCommGroup W] [Module A W]
    (l : ℤ) (x y h : Module.End A W) (f : ℕ → W) : Prop :=
  x (f 0) = 0 ∧
  (∀ i : ℕ, i < l.toNat → x (f (i+1)) = ((l : A) - (i : A)) • f i) ∧
  (∀ i : ℕ, i < l.toNat → y (f i) = ((i : A) + 1) • f (i+1)) ∧
  y (f l.toNat) = 0 ∧
  (∀ i : ℕ, i ≤ l.toNat → h (f i) = ((l : A) - 2 * (i : A)) • f i)
def basisFacts (l : ℤ) (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) : Prop :=
  0 ≤ l ∧ 0 < l + 1 ∧ 0 < l.toNat + 1 ∧ Fintype.card (Ind l) = l.toNat + 1 ∧
  (∃ b : Basis (Ind l) ℂ V, ∀ i, b i = e y v i.val) ∧
  strings l x y h v ∧
  (∀ t : ℕ, l.toNat + 1 ≤ t → (y ^ t) v = 0) ∧
  generatorFormulas l x y h (e y v) ∧
  (∀ (r : ℕ) (i : Ind l),
    divided x r (e y v i.val) =
      if r ≤ i.val then (Nat.choose (l.toNat - i.val + r) r : ℂ) • e y v (i.val-r) else 0) ∧
  (∀ (r : ℕ) (i : Ind l),
    divided y r (e y v i.val) =
      if i.val + r ≤ l.toNat then (Nat.choose (i.val+r) r : ℂ) • e y v (i.val+r) else 0)

instance locRatComplexTower (p : ℕ) : IsScalarTower (loc p) ℚ ℂ :=
  IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq' rfl
def locSpec (p : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ q : ℚ, q ∈ loc p ↔ ∃ a d : ℤ, ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ d ∧ q = (a : ℚ) / (d : ℚ)
def latticeFacts (p : ℕ) (l : ℤ) (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Prop :=
  locSpec p ∧ Nonempty (IntegralOps x y h M) ∧
  (∀ A : IntegralOps x y h M,
    A.ih * A.ix - A.ix * A.ih = (2 : ℤ) • A.ix ∧
    A.ih * A.iy - A.iy * A.ih = (-2 : ℤ) • A.iy ∧
    A.ix * A.iy - A.iy * A.ix = A.ih) ∧
  Function.Injective (iota p M) ∧
  Nonempty (Basis (Ind l) (loc p) (MR p M)) ∧
  Module.finrank (loc p) (MR p M) = l.toNat + 1 ∧
  Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range (iota p M)) = ⊤ ∧
  ∀ (r : ℕ) (z : V), z ∈ (iota p M).range →
    divided x r z ∈ (iota p M).range ∧ divided y r z ∈ (iota p M).range
def matrixFacts (p : ℕ) (l : ℤ) (x y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Prop :=
  ∀ b : Basis (Ind l) ℂ V, (∀ i, b i = e y v i.val) →
  ∀ i j : Ind l,
    IsUnit (Nat.choose l.toNat j.val : loc p) ∧
    (Nat.choose l.toNat j.val : ℚ)⁻¹ ∈ loc p ∧
    (∀ z ∈ (iota p M).range, matrixUnit b i j z ∈ (iota p M).range) ∧
    matrixUnit b i j = (Nat.choose l.toNat j.val : ℂ)⁻¹ •
      (divided x (l.toNat-i.val) * divided y l.toNat * divided x l.toNat * divided y (l.toNat-j.val)) ∧
    divided y l.toNat * divided x l.toNat = matrixUnit b (Fin.last l.toNat) (Fin.last l.toNat) ∧
    divided x (l.toNat-i.val) * matrixUnit b (Fin.last l.toNat) (Fin.last l.toNat) =
      matrixUnit b i (Fin.last l.toNat) ∧
    matrixUnit b (Fin.last l.toNat) (Fin.last l.toNat) * divided y (l.toNat-j.val) =
      (Nat.choose l.toNat j.val : ℂ) • matrixUnit b (Fin.last l.toNat) j
def localizationFacts (p : ℕ) (l : ℤ) (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Prop :=
  latticeFacts p l x y h M ∧ matrixFacts p l x y v M
def coordinateFacts (p : ℕ) (l : ℤ) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Prop :=
  (∀ i : Ind l, Jcoord p M y v i.val = Jcoord p M y v 0) ∧
  Jcoord p M y v 0 ≠ ⊥ ∧ (Jcoord p M y v 0).FG ∧
  ∃ d : (Ind l → Jcoord p M y v 0) ≃ₗ[loc p] (iota p M).range,
    ∀ c, (d c : V) = ∑ i : Ind l, (c i : ℂ) • e y v i.val
def rationalMu (p : ℕ) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (M : Submodule ℤ V) :
    ℚ ⊗[loc p] (Jcoord p M y v 0) →ₗ[ℚ] ℂ :=
  LinearMap.liftBaseChange ℚ (Jcoord p M y v 0).subtype
def rationalFacts (p : ℕ) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Prop :=
  FiniteDimensional ℚ (ℚ ⊗[loc p] (Jcoord p M y v 0)) ∧
  Module.finrank ℚ (ℚ ⊗[loc p] (Jcoord p M y v 0)) = 1 ∧
  Function.Injective (rationalMu p y v M)
def principalFacts (p : ℕ) (l : ℤ) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Prop :=
  ∃ b : ℂ, b ≠ 0 ∧ b ∈ Jcoord p M y v 0 ∧
    Jcoord p M y v 0 = Submodule.span (loc p) ({b} : Set ℂ) ∧
    ∃ a : Basis (Ind l) (loc p) (MR p M), ∀ i, iota p M (a i) = b • e y v i.val
def commonFacts (p : ℕ) (l : ℤ) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Prop :=
  coordinateFacts p l y v M ∧ rationalFacts p y v M ∧ principalFacts p l y v M
def scalarFacts (p : ℕ) (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Prop :=
  ∃ (bar : loc p →+* K) (eps : ZMod p →+* K),
    (∀ (a d : ℤ) (hd : ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ d) (r : loc p),
      (r : ℚ) = (a : ℚ) / (d : ℚ) → bar r = (a : K) / (d : K)) ∧
    (letI : Algebra (loc p) K := bar.toAlgebra
     letI : Algebra (ZMod p) K := eps.toAlgebra
     ∃ (Phi : VK K M ≃ₗ[K] (K ⊗[loc p] MR p M))
       (Psi : (K ⊗[loc p] MR p M) ≃ₗ[K] (K ⊗[ZMod p] ModN (MR p M) p)),
       (∀ (c : K) (m : M), Phi (c ⊗ₜ[ℤ] m) = c ⊗ₜ[loc p] (1 ⊗ₜ[ℤ] m)) ∧
       (∀ (c : K) (s : loc p) (m : M),
         Phi.symm (c ⊗ₜ[loc p] (s ⊗ₜ[ℤ] m)) = (c * bar s) ⊗ₜ[ℤ] m) ∧
       (∀ (c : K) (u : MR p M), Psi (c ⊗ₜ[loc p] u) = c ⊗ₜ[ZMod p] ModN.mkQ p u) ∧
       (∀ (c : K) (u : MR p M), Psi.symm (c ⊗ₜ[ZMod p] ModN.mkQ p u) = c ⊗ₜ[loc p] u) ∧
       ∀ f : Module.End ℤ M,
         Phi.toLinearMap.comp (f.baseChange K) =
           ((f.baseChange (loc p)).baseChange K).comp Phi.toLinearMap ∧
         ∃ F : Module.End (ZMod p) (ModN (MR p M) p),
           (∀ u : MR p M, F (ModN.mkQ p u) = ModN.mkQ p (f.baseChange (loc p) u)) ∧
           Psi.toLinearMap.comp ((f.baseChange (loc p)).baseChange K) =
             (F.baseChange K).comp Psi.toLinearMap)
def extendBasis {A W : Type*} [Semiring A] [AddCommMonoid W] [Module A W]
    (l : ℤ) (b : Basis (Ind l) A W) (i : ℕ) : W :=
  if hi : i < l.toNat+1 then b ⟨i,hi⟩ else 0
def reductionWitness (p : ℕ) (l : ℤ) (K : Type*) [Field K]
    {x y h : Module.End ℂ V} {M : Submodule ℤ V} (A : IntegralOps x y h M)
    (beta : Basis (Ind l) K (VK K M)) (T : Ind l → Ind l → Module.End K (VK K M)) : Prop :=
  Module.finrank K (VK K M) = l.toNat+1 ∧ 0 < l.toNat+1 ∧
  generatorFormulas l (A.ix.baseChange K) (A.iy.baseChange K) (A.ih.baseChange K) (extendBasis l beta) ∧
  (∀ i j k : Ind l, T i j (beta k) = if k = j then beta i else 0) ∧
  (∀ i j : Ind l, (Nat.choose l.toNat j.val : K) ≠ 0 ∧
    T i j = (Nat.choose l.toNat j.val : K)⁻¹ •
      ((A.iX (l.toNat-i.val)).baseChange K * (A.iY l.toNat).baseChange K *
        (A.iX l.toNat).baseChange K * (A.iY (l.toNat-j.val)).baseChange K)) ∧
  ∀ r : ℕ, r ≤ l.toNat →
    (r.factorial : K) ≠ 0 ∧
    (A.iX r).baseChange K = (r.factorial : K)⁻¹ • (A.ix.baseChange K)^r ∧
    (A.iY r).baseChange K = (r.factorial : K)⁻¹ • (A.iy.baseChange K)^r
def reductionFacts (p : ℕ) (l : ℤ) (K : Type*) [Field K]
    (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Prop :=
  scalarFacts p K M ∧
  ∀ A : IntegralOps x y h M, ∃ beta T, reductionWitness p l K A beta T
def invariantFacts (p : ℕ) (l : ℤ) (K : Type*) [Field K]
    (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Prop :=
  Nontrivial (VK K M) ∧
  ∀ A : IntegralOps x y h M, ∃ beta T, reductionWitness p l K A beta T ∧
    ∀ W : Submodule K (VK K M),
      stable W (A.ix.baseChange K) → stable W (A.iy.baseChange K) →
      stable W (A.ih.baseChange K) → ∀ i j : Ind l, stable W (T i j)
def endpoint (K : Type*) [Field K] (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Prop :=
  ∃ A : IntegralOps x y h M, Nontrivial (VK K M) ∧
    ∀ W : Submodule K (VK K M),
      stable W (A.ix.baseChange K) → stable W (A.iy.baseChange K) →
      stable W (A.ih.baseChange K) → W = ⊥ ∨ W = ⊤
end Reduction

premises.statement: The field K has characteristic p.
With the representation act, V=V(lambda) is the complex irreducible highest-weight sl2(C)-module of highest weight lambda and has complex dimension lambda+1.
L=sl2(C), and x,y,h are its Chevalley generators, satisfying [h,x]=2x, [h,y]=-2y and [x,y]=h.
v is nonzero, xv=0, and hv=lambda v.
premises.type: v0 ≠ 0 ∧ act x v0 = 0 ∧ act h v0 = (l : ℂ) • v0

premises.statement: M is an admissible lattice in V: it is a free abelian subgroup possessing an integer basis which is also a complex basis of V, and is stable under U_Z. M is arbitrary and is not assumed to be the minimal lattice.

P.explanation: The original integer prime is positive, so using p:Nat with Nat.Prime p and CharP K p preserves exactly its domain; l:Z and 0≤l

conclusion.statement: V_K is nonzero, and for every K-linear subspace W of V_K, if W is invariant under x_K,y_K,h_K (the action rho of the Chevalley generators of L_K), then W={0} or W=V_K. Thus V(K) is irreducible as an L(K)-module.
conclusion.type: Reduction.endpoint K (act x) (act y) (act h) M

representation:
Use the concrete complex trace-zero 2×2 matrix Lie algebra Reduction.SL for the source's L=sl2(C), with a Lie homomorphism act into complex endomorphisms and an arbitrary generating Chevalley triple x,y,h. The pinned IsSl2Triple includes h≠0 and the three commutator relations; the span condition says the triple generates the whole complex Lie algebra. H004 retains finite dimension, nonzeroness, irreducibility under every Lie element and existence of a highest-weight vector of weight l; H006 fixes the source's chosen vector. The prime p is represented by a natural number, equivalently the original positive prime integer; the weight l remains an integer. Under H003, Ind l=Fin(l.toNat+1) is exactly the ordered set of integers 0≤i≤l. basisFacts explicitly retains nonnegativity and l+1>0, so later consumers do not rely on an unstated conversion. Fin indices are natural positions, subtraction in divided-power indices is truncated natural subtraction in regions where it equals the source's nonnegative integer difference. Complex weights such as l−2i use signed casts.
M is an arbitrary integer submodule of V, equivalently an additive subgroup. admissible expresses an integer basis whose inclusions form a complex basis and preservation by all divided powers. Preservation by these generators is equivalent to preservation by their unital integer algebra U_Z. No special choice of lattice is built into a definition. divided is the action of x^r/r! or y^r/r! as a complex endomorphism, using endomorphism multiplication as composition. matrixUnit b i j sends w to its j-th basis coordinate times b_i. It is only used with an actual basis whose values equal the source e_i; no basis is selected by an unproved definition.
loc p is the subring of Q generated by inverses of integers prime to p. The typed locSpec obligation in T003 identifies it with the exact fractions a/d, p∤d from D007; this identification is proved, not assumed. The composite inclusion loc p→Q→C gives all localized actions. MR is R⊗_Z M, and iota is the balanced multiplication map from LinearMap.liftBaseChange. Jcoord is the inverse image of its range under c↦c e_i; rationalMu is multiplication Q⊗_R J→C. coordinateFacts gives the exact direct-sum isomorphism with its sum formula, rationalFacts includes finite dimensionality as well as finrank=1 and injectivity, and principalFacts supplies the scalar b and actual localized basis. Module.finrank is Cardinal.toNat of rank: it is used as dimension only with the explicit finite basis or finite-dimensional conditions.
Use the standard scalar-first tensor convention VK=K⊗_Z M throughout. The source writes M⊗_Z K; the canonical symmetry sends c⊗m to m⊗c, identifies K scalar multiplication on the first factor with that on the second, and identifies f.baseChange K with the source action on pure tensors. This is an order convention for one representation, not a second independent model. T008 explicitly constructs the source's substantive scalar-extension and reduction bridges, in this convention. ModN(MR,p) is the quotient by the range of integer multiplication by p, which is exactly pMR, with its canonical ZMod p module. The existential ring homomorphisms bar and eps supply the actual R and prime-field scalar actions on K; they are conclusions, never premise instances. Pure-tensor forward and inverse formulas and intertwining obligations fix the meanings of both bridges.
IntegralOps contains only integer-linear restrictions with equality to the complex operators after inclusion; existence is proved in T003. Their components are unique by injectivity of inclusion of M, so all compatible bundles induce the same operators on VK. This avoids any definition choosing restrictions before their existence is proved. reductionFacts quantifies over every compatible bundle and supplies the basis, matrix units, nonzero binomials and factorial power identities. Invariant subspaces are actual Submodule K objects; stable means closure under the stated operator. The endpoint existentially supplies the canonical restriction bundle, nonzeroness and the complete zero-or-top assertion. No Lie algebra of trace-zero matrices over K is substituted for the integral Chevalley construction: in characteristic two the three integral generators are still the ones whose induced actions occur here.
